correctness.rationale: A B-before-A geodesic exists, so puncturing the cube leaves distance n between endpoints. All shortest routes flip each label once and changing one intermediate vertex exchanges adjacent flips. A route is forbidden exactly when all A labels precede all B labels. Every valid ordering can bubble all B labels left without losing its cross inversion, then sort within blocks, proving connectivity. The k!(n−k)! forbidden permutations each have exactly one edge to a valid neighbor, by swapping across the block boundary; the neighbor uniquely recovers its forbidden predecessor. The degree and edge counts follow, including the single degree-zero vertex at n=2. For a singleton A, inserting the non-A first target label never places A first; the rest of adjacent insertion realizes Kendall distance. Reversal handles singleton B. In the interior four-label witness the two fixed A-before-B orders make the initial and final opposite cross inversions mutually exclusive. A four-swap path could change only discordant pairs and would have to lose one cross inversion before obtaining the other; all external labels retain their orders, so the intervening state is forbidden. Parity rules out length five, and the six displayed adjacent swaps retain at least one cross inversion at every step. Independent direct enumeration of cube vertex sequences corroborated counts, both extreme-layer isometries, and the existence of distance-4-versus-6 pairs through n=6; the proof establishes all n.
residual_risks: The proof does not upper-bound the excess for arbitrary pairs at interior layers.
